Dockerfile.text:
FROM node:22-alpine
WORKDIR /app
COPY cron.mjs monitor.mjs notify.mjs dashboard.mjs server.mjs ./
RUN mkdir /data && chown node /data
USER node
ENV PORT=8080 STATE=/data/state.json
VOLUME /data
EXPOSE 8080
HEALTHCHECK CMD wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:8080/healthz || exit 1
CMD ["node", "server.mjs"]

README.md.text:
# cron-heartbeat

After using this, you can now **find out within minutes when a cron job stops
running or starts failing**, which used to mean noticing a missing backup weeks
later.

**Live tool:** https://duncan-haywood.github.io/monorepo-projects/cron-heartbeat/

Two parts, both free and with no account:

- **`index.html`** — paste a crontab, get next runs, the longest healthy
  silence, a suggested grace period, a wrapped command line that reports exit
  status, and a `checks.json`. Runs in the browser; nothing is uploaded.
- **`server.mjs`** — a heartbeat monitor ("dead man's switch") in one Node file
  with no dependencies. Jobs ping `/ping/<name>` (or `/start`, `/fail`); when a
  ping does not arrive by the next scheduled run plus grace, it alerts a
  webhook (Slack/Discord/Mattermost style) and/or an ntfy topic, once, and
  again when the job recovers.

```
CONFIG=example-checks.json PING_KEY=secret ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL=... node server.mjs
node --test
```

## What the monitor does

- **Dashboard** at `/` (needs your key): every check's state, reason and last ping.
- **Public status page** at `/s`, off by default (`PUBLIC_STATUS=1`): names and
  operational/disruption only, no keys, timings or reasons. Title: `STATUS_TITLE`.
- **Maintenance pause**: `/pause/<name>` and `/resume/<name>` (key required) stop and restart
  alerting for one check. Resuming restarts its clock, so the paused time never alerts.
- **Status badge** at `/badge/<name>.svg` (with `PUBLIC_STATUS=1`): an embeddable
  operational / disruption / paused SVG, same disclosure as `/s`.
- **History** at `/history/<name>`: the last 50 pings and alerts per check.
- **Alerts, any mix of**: webhook (Slack/Discord/Mattermost), ntfy, Telegram bot
  (`TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`, `TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID`), email through your own Resend
  account (`RESEND_API_KEY`, `ALERT_EMAIL_TO`, `ALERT_EMAIL_FROM`). One channel
  failing does not stop the others; if all fail it retries next tick.
- **Persistent state** (`STATE`, default `/data/state.json` in Docker, written
  atomically and flushed on shutdown), so a restart does not forget your jobs.
- The key can be sent as `?key=` or `Authorization: Bearer <key>`; pings accept GET or POST.

## Deploy your own copy (nothing runs on the author's side)

A monitor must stay awake and remember state, so every route below gives it a disk and one always-on instance.

- **Render**: fork this repository, open `https://render.com/deploy?repo=<your fork URL>`.
  `render.yaml` builds the `Dockerfile` on the paid *starter* plan (about $7/month, your account)
  with a 1 GB disk and a generated `PING_KEY`. Then set `CHECKS_JSON` and an alert channel in
  the environment tab.
- **Fly.io**: `fly.toml` has the exact commands in its header (volume, secrets, `fly deploy`).
- **Any Docker host**: `PING_KEY=change-me docker compose up -d` (see `docker-compose.yml`).

Ping with `https://<your-service>/ping/<name>?key=<PING_KEY>`; `/healthz` is open for health checks.
Do not use Render's free plan for real monitoring: it sleeps when idle and has no disk.

Files: `cron.mjs` (parser, next-run, evaluate), `monitor.mjs` (alert state
machine, history), `notify.mjs` (alert channels), `dashboard.mjs` (HTML),
`crontab.mjs` (crontab to entries/config), `server.mjs` (HTTP shell),
`usage.mjs` (opt-out local counters).

Timezones: UTC by default. Set `"tz": "Europe/London"` on a check, or put `CRON_TZ=Europe/London` above jobs in the crontab tool, and the schedule is read in that IANA zone. Same as Vixie cron on daylight-saving days: a repeated wall-clock hour counts once, and a time that does not exist (spring forward) is skipped that day, so a missed run on that one day is not detected. The host timezone is never consulted.

Limits, stated plainly: five-field cron plus `@daily`-style macros
(no `@reboot`, no `L`/`W`/`#`); no per-check alert routing or teams; the
monitor is a single process, so run it on a different machine from the jobs
it watches. Not a substitute for real alerting on critical systems.

VENTURE.yaml.text:
name: cron-heartbeat
description: >-
  Free dead-man's-switch monitoring for cron jobs: a browser tool that turns a
  pasted crontab into next runs, a grace period, a success/failure-reporting
  command line and a config, plus a zero-dependency self-hosted Node monitor
  that alerts a webhook or ntfy topic when a job goes quiet or fails.
stage: prototype
owner: duncan

# Screened 2026-10-08. Paid market is real: Healthchecks.io, Cronitor, Dead Man's
# Snitch and Better Stack heartbeats charge roughly $5-30 a month and gate the
# useful limits (check count, alert channels) behind plans. A self-hostable
# single file with a crontab-to-config helper serves the developer who will not
# pay per check and will not run a Django app.
# duplicate_check.py top score 0.20 (vendor-watch, a page differ, not a job
# monitor).
#
# First visitor: sysadmins and indie developers on r/selfhosted, r/sysadmin,
# r/devops and Hacker News asking "how do I know my cron job ran", "cron
# monitoring self hosted", "healthchecks.io alternative", "dead man's switch cron".
# Volume not measured with an external tool.
#
# Path to revenue (payments stay off): free tool and open-source monitor as a
# lead magnet; if repeat use shows up, a hosted version with email alerts and a
# status page is the natural paid step -- owner-gated (billing, hosting under
# the public name).

hypotheses:
  - claim: >-
      Developers who run a handful of cron jobs on their own boxes will paste a
      crontab into a private browser tool and then actually self-host the
      monitor, because the free hosted tiers cap check count and alert channels.
    status: untested
    checked: null
    evidence: customer-contact
  - claim: >-
      Reporting exit status (the /fail ping) rather than only silence is what
      makes users keep the wrapped lines in their crontab after the first week.
    status: untested
    checked: null
    evidence: customer-contact

economics:
  currency: USD
  mrr: null
  monthly_cost: 0
  customers: null

budget:
  monthly_cap: 1
  protected: true

kill_criteria:
  - Fewer than three distinct GitHub users (issues, stars, or a paste-in report) engage with the tool within 90 days of it being reachable from the published site.
  - A user reports a missed alert or a wrong next-run time, at which point the scheduler maths or the alert state machine needs revisiting before anything else.

links:
  production: https://duncan-haywood.github.io/monorepo-projects/cron-heartbeat/
  analytics: null

fly.toml.text:
# Fly.io self-deploy, in your own account (needs flyctl and a card on file with Fly):
#   fly launch --copy-config --no-deploy --dockerfile Dockerfile
#   fly volumes create state --size 1
#   fly secrets set PING_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16) CHECKS_JSON="$(cat example-checks.json)"
#   fly secrets set ALERT_NTFY_URL=https://ntfy.sh/your-topic   # or any channel in notify.mjs
#   fly deploy
# One machine that never auto-stops: a monitor must stay awake to alert.
app = "cron-heartbeat-CHANGE-ME"
primary_region = "iad"

[build]
  dockerfile = "Dockerfile"

[env]
  PORT = "8080"
  STATE = "/data/state.json"

[mounts]
  source = "state"
  destination = "/data"

[http_service]
  internal_port = 8080
  force_https = true
  auto_stop_machines = "off"
  auto_start_machines = false
  min_machines_running = 1
  [[http_service.checks]]
    path = "/healthz"
    interval = "30s"
    timeout = "5s"

index.html.text:
Know when your cron jobs silently stop

Cron tells you nothing when the server is down, the crontab was overwritten or a job hangs. Paste your crontab: get next runs, the longest healthy silence, a sensible grace period, a wrapped line that reports success or failure, and the config for a heartbeat monitor you run yourself — one Node file, no dependencies, no account.

Your crontab

Jobs

checks.json for the monitor


    
  


  

    
Run the monitor

    
curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Duncan-Haywood/fp-monorepo/main/ventures/cron-heartbeat/{server,monitor,cron}.mjs
CONFIG=checks.json PING_KEY=choose-a-secret \
ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL=https://hooks.slack.com/... node server.mjs

    
Put it behind HTTPS (Caddy or nginx) on a box that is not the one running the jobs. Alerts go only to the webhook or ALERT_NTFY_URL topic you set. State is a JSON file next to it. Pings accept GET or POST at /ping/<name>, /ping/<name>/start and /ping/<name>/fail; /status returns every check as JSON. Add ?key= to each URL when PING_KEY is set.

  


  

    
Questions

    
How do I know if a cron job stopped running?

    
Cron only reports errors it can mail, and silently does nothing when the machine is down, the crontab is overwritten or the job hangs. A heartbeat (dead man's switch) inverts this: the job pings a URL when it succeeds, and the monitor alerts when the ping does not arrive within the schedule plus a grace period.

    
What grace period should I use?

    
Long enough to cover normal run time and scheduler jitter, short enough that a missed run is noticed while it still matters. This tool suggests about 10% of the typical interval, between 1 minute and 1 hour; raise it for jobs that take a long time to finish.

    
Does it report failures as well as silence?

    
Yes. The wrapped command pings /ping/name when the job exits 0 and /ping/name/fail when it does not. A /start ping is also supported so a job that starts and never finishes is distinguished from one that never started.

    
What does the monitor store, and what does it cost?

    
It is one Node.js file with no dependencies that keeps check names and last-ping times in a JSON file on your own machine. Alerts go only to the webhook or ntfy topic you configure. There is no account and no cost; you pay only for the box it runs on.

    
Which timezone does it use?

    
UTC by default. Put a CRON_TZ=Europe/London line above a job in the pasted crontab, or set "tz" on a check, and the schedule is read in that zone, daylight saving included: a repeated hour counts once and a skipped hour is skipped that day. The host timezone is never used. See also the Cron DST Drift Check.

  


  

    
No warranty. This tool and the monitor are provided free and as-is, without warranty of any kind, express or implied, and with no uptime or delivery guarantee. A monitor can itself fail or miss an alert; it is not legal, tax, or financial advice and should not be your only safeguard for critical systems. Everything on this page runs in your browser: your crontab is never uploaded and the page makes no network requests. Hosted on a free static site with no SLA. Usage counters (opt-out below) stay in your browser's local storage.

render.yaml.text:
# One-click self-deploy: https://render.com/deploy?repo=<your fork URL>
# Render builds the Dockerfile in YOUR account; nothing runs on the author's.
# Paid "starter" plan on purpose: the free plan sleeps when idle and has no disk, and a
# monitor that sleeps misses the alerts it exists to send. Set CHECKS_JSON after deploy.
services:
  - type: web
    name: cron-heartbeat
    runtime: docker
    dockerContext: ventures/cron-heartbeat
    dockerfilePath: ventures/cron-heartbeat/Dockerfile
    plan: starter
    healthCheckPath: /healthz
    disk:
      name: state
      mountPath: /data
      sizeGB: 1
    envVars:
      - key: PING_KEY
        generateValue: true
      - key: CHECKS_JSON
        value: '{"example":{"periodSeconds":86400,"graceSeconds":3600}}'
      - key: PUBLIC_STATUS
        value: "0"
      - key: ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL
        sync: false
      - key: ALERT_NTFY_URL
        sync: false
      - key: TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN
        sync: false
      - key: TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID
        sync: false
      - key: RESEND_API_KEY
        sync: false
      - key: ALERT_EMAIL_TO
        sync: false
      - key: ALERT_EMAIL_FROM
        sync: false
